source_text.body:
Tidy notes and make Anki flashcards
The author uses Claude Desktop with Obsidian and Anki MCP integrations; Claude writes a plan, he approves it, and Claude tidies notes and creates flashcards.
·
Nov 14, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The author connects Claude Desktop to Obsidian and Anki through MCP servers. He sets up a project with instructions covering card rules, cloze preference, and a card format. He points Claude at specific Obsidian notes or an Anki deck. Claude writes a plan under an Anki Notes page, he approves it, and Claude carries it out while tracking progress there.
How it went
The source gives no numbers or measured results. It describes the workflow as working for him. Claude tidies the notes, makes cloze-style cards, and drops cards it judges low-value.
Worth knowing
Tracking progress in an Obsidian page lets you start a fresh chat and resume when a large deck overflows the context.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Look at my notes on [topic or folder] in Obsidian and first write me a plan for how you would tidy them: fix headings, merge duplicates, and add links. Wait for my approval. Then apply the changes and create Anki flashcards in the deck [deck name] for the key facts, and finish by listing what you changed and how many cards you created.
Original source: https://codecraftsphere.substack.com/p/how-i-finally-built-a-knowledge-system?r=2c2vs2
